justification: A uses bold sans headings with section numbers, so the hierarchy reads strongly against the serif body (A1, A2). B's light, unnumbered serif headings are weak and lean on red rules to carry structure (B1, B2). B's narrow body text sits close in size to the headings, and its header band and red rules feel slightly fussy. A's running header and footer give the document a more finished feel. Tables and layout are otherwise much the same.

A keeps the allocation table whole on one page (A2). B splits a five-row table across B2 and B3 and repeats the caption, which fragments the data. A's charts come right after the table. A's last page is mostly empty (A4), but B's fuller pages are not enough to make up for the broken table.

A packs content into four well-filled pages: the bar chart stays with its table on A2, and the cash-flow section and appendix share A4. B pushes the bar chart onto B3, away from its table. It leaves half of B2 and most of B5 empty, which makes the pacing uneven. B's dark header and footer bands and numbered headings add navigation, but they weigh the pages down. A's indented body text under hanging rule-topped headings reads more refined.

A leaves most of its pages empty. The cover is mostly blank below the mission text, and page 4 holds only a small table at the top. The title also breaks awkwardly, leaving the Arabic stranded on its own line. B fits the content into three pages: the image sits on the cover, the stats and programmes share a page, and the table follows the finance text directly. The cost is an orphaned Arabic line at the top of B3. B's Arabic is larger and easier to read. A's serif English pairing is slightly more refined.

A pairs a bold sans heading with a serif body for clear hierarchy, keeps the bar chart with its table on A2, and fills pages evenly. B uses light-weight headings that read weaker. Its chart is split from its table across B1–B2. B also leaves large empty areas on B2 and B4, where the appendix is stranded alone. B's header and footer bands are polished, but they do not offset the uneven page flow.

B keeps the allocation table whole on one page (B2), while A splits it across pages with the repeated header and leaves the total stranded on A3. A has a fuller final page with the image, whereas B4 is mostly empty. Even so, the intact table and the coherent chart-and-image flow on B3 outweigh that.

A opens with a dedicated full-bleed illustrated cover and a clean title band, and its bold sans headings give clear contrast with the serif body text. B's title wraps awkwardly, leaving the Arabic word stranded on its own line. B also repeats the cover image directly below the mission text. A's English paragraph orphans across pages (A2–A3), but B similarly splits the Arabic school-visits text onto page 3. The tables are equivalent.

A uses sans text and heavy teal header bands that give its sections strong hierarchy, and its cover splits image and title cleanly. However, A4 is mostly empty, holding two short rows, and A3 has a gap below its text. B overlays the title on a cohesive full-bleed cover (B1) and uses lighter rule-based section heads. Its pages are more evenly filled: B4 carries the replanting text plus next steps. The B3 figure is full-width with a balanced caption. Overall B reads as more refined and better paced.

A keeps the allocation table intact on A2. B splits it across B2–B3, repeating the header, which hurts the tables score. A's refined serif with matched Arabic and its thin rule-headed sections read more elegantly. B's heavy full-bleed bands are bolder, but its denser text and table break make it feel clunkier. A4 is sparse but cleaner overall.

B's serif text is set less justified, with fewer rivers than A's tight justified sans text. Its charts are larger and fill the pages better (B3, B4), leaving less dead space than A's squat charts (A2, A3), so its pages feel better balanced. A is more compact, but it leaves large empty bottoms. Both use the same tables and blank final pages.

A splits the income statement across pages A4–A5 with a repeated header, which fragments the table. A's callout box also covers the building illustration on A6. B keeps both financial tables together on B6. B places its pull quote beside the image on B7, uses consistent header and footer bands, and gives the cover a cohesive blue title band (B1). B's section divider pages (B2, B5) are mostly empty and slightly wasteful, but they do provide clear navigation. A is more compact and its hierarchy is a little tighter, yet B is cleaner overall.

A leaves most of its pages empty. The cover is about two-thirds blank. The finance table sits alone on a mostly empty fourth page. The mission column is oddly indented away from its heading. The callout box on page 3 overlaps the illustration awkwardly. B packs the same content into three well-balanced pages. Its columns align with the headings. The brown callout sits cleanly beside the image. The table follows its section text directly, and running headers give steady rhythm. A's serif headings are a little more refined, but B's layout is clearly stronger.

A is compact and consistent: every section opens with the same ruled heading and body on one page. B adds divider pages with an awkward sidebar and broken bilingual titles. It also handles headings inconsistently: Chair's statement and Finance content pages have no heading, while Operations and People do. Its heavy header and footer bands are cramped. B's dividers mostly hold empty space, so the document reads disjointedly.

A keeps the content to four pages with consistent teal section bands and a compact image on A3. B leaves a large empty gap on B3 because the image is pushed to B4, then strands a single paragraph on B5 that is otherwise blank. That orphaned final page and the uneven pacing make B weaker. Its serif text and hairline headings are refined but carry less hierarchy.

B's cover title keeps the English name on one line with the Arabic beneath, where A breaks the bilingual title awkwardly across three lines. B's Latin and Arabic faces pair more harmoniously. B's overlaid callout box on the image reads as more refined than A's split panel. A's bolder serif body is slightly more readable, but B is the cleaner overall.

A presents a proper illustrated cover and then sets the content on two pages with even density. Its sections, stats row and table sit together with the text they belong to. B leaves most of page B1 empty after a single short paragraph. On B4 the finance table is stranded alone at the top, separated from its section on B3. The title in B1 also breaks awkwardly across lines. A's one flaw is a programmes paragraph that runs over from A2 to A3, which is a smaller problem than B's empty pages and orphaned table.

A uses bold, numbered sans headings over a serif body, which gives clear section hierarchy. B's headings are light-weight and barely stronger than its thin body text. B's appendix heading is even smaller than its other headings, which weakens hierarchy further. B's charts are squashed flat, and the cash cover line loses its detail. A gives its charts adequate height. B's cover band is efficient, but A's full title page and steadier section rhythm read better. A's thin title page is a minor cost.

A pairs a bold sans heading face with a serif body, so the section heads (Recommendation, Options considered) stand out clearly from the body text. Its indented body gives a hanging-head structure that is easy to scan. B uses a light serif for its section heads, which looks weaker against the body text. B's full-width justified lines are long and show wide gaps (B1, B2). B does have a tidier single-line title and a cleaner table. On balance, A's hierarchy and readability edge ahead.

A keeps the allocation table whole on A2, where B splits it across B2–B3 with a repeated header. B's strong section bands, running headers and contained image give a clear structure. A leaves a nearly empty page A5 and large voids on A3, and its full-bleed image on A4 floats awkwardly. B fits the content into four well-filled pages with even rhythm.

The two designs share a near-identical layout. A uses a crisp sans with bold, heavy headline figures. Its page 2 carries a running header band naming the section, which helps orientation. B's serif is elegant but lighter and smaller on screen, and its KPI labels are faint. B's page 2 has only a thin red rule with no running header. A's "phase two." line orphans a word, a minor flaw.

A keeps the allocation table whole on one page (A2), while B splits it across pages B2–B3 with a repeated header, breaking comparison of totals. B's full-bleed section bands give strong structure but are heavy and repetitive. A's charts sit above their section heading, and its last page is half empty (A4), but the table integrity matters more.

A gives each section its own page with consistent headers, keeps the income statement whole on A4, and pairs charts with Operations on A3. B splits the income statement across B4 and B5 with a repeated header, leaves B2 half-empty, and detaches the Operations stats from their section, so the pacing is uneven. B's cover and dark bands are clean, but A's navy palette and running headers read as more coherent.

A is compact and consistent over three pages. Its mission sits with the image on the cover, and its stats and programmes share page 2. The finance table stays with its heading on page 3. B leaves most of page 1 empty and pushes the hero image onto page 2. Its section headings hang outdented at an odd left margin. B's finance table is orphaned on page 4, separated from its heading. B also places its quote box over the illustration, hiding part of it.

B keeps the income statement in one table on B4, where A splits it across A4–A5 and repeats the header. A also leaves the chair's statement page (A2) mostly empty. B's Arabic body is set at a matching, more legible size and its pages fill more evenly (B2, B3). Its consistent gold header band gives steadier rhythm. A's cover image is brighter, but its headline sits in plain white space.

A keeps its content compact across three pages. The cover carries the image, and the finance table sits with its heading. B leaves most of page 1 empty and pushes the first image onto page 2. Its table is orphaned on page 4, which is nearly blank. B's section headings also hang outdented past the text margin, and its Arabic text is noticeably smaller than the English.

The two designs share the same structure. A's serif face reads as more refined and suits a board decision paper. Its slightly more generous margins ease the dense body text. B's sans is clean but lightly tracked and justified, which leaves loose word spacing (B1 closing line, B2). B's running header band is a useful touch, but it does not outweigh A's better text setting.

A uses bold numbered section headings that stand out clearly, and its body text is larger and more legible. Its cover pairs a bright illustration with a solid title band. B's light, thin headings are weaker, and its small, light serif body text is harder to read. B's dark, muddy cover has low contrast in the moon and subtitle. B's gold rules and header ornament add some polish, but the overall hierarchy is softer.

A gives each section its own page with a consistent opening rule and heading, so Finance and its tables sit together (A4) and People and safety keeps its image with its text (A5). B packs sections in continuously, which strands the Finance intro at the foot of B3 with its tables on B4. It also pushes the People section to the bottom of B4, leaves an orphaned image page with a large empty area (B5), and adds heavy header and footer bands. A's serif body text and lighter header read more refined. B's cover image is stronger, but A's overall rhythm is better.

B gives each section its own page, so the Finance heading and text sit with their tables (B4) and People and safety stays with its apprenticeship panel (B5). A splits Finance across pages: the heading is at the bottom of A3 and the tables open A4 without a heading. People and safety then runs over into a mostly empty A5. A's bold sans in the headers and bands is crisper, but B's section flow and running heads are more coherent.

A uses consistent teal header bands and running heads, giving clear section rhythm, and it fits in four pages. B keeps its table whole on B2, while A splits it across A2–A3 with a repeated header. But B's charts sit orphaned at the top of B3 above a mostly empty page, its full-bleed image on B4 breaks rhythm, and B5 strands a single paragraph on a nearly blank page. B's small rule-based headings also carry weaker hierarchy.

A leaves large empty areas: the cover band is followed by a mostly blank page (A1), and the finance table sits alone on a nearly empty page (A4). Its Arabic title also wraps awkwardly. B uses a full-bleed cover image with a clean brown title band (B1). Its numbered sections run continuously, and the table stays with its finance section (B3). B's one weakness is a short paragraph split across a page break (B2–B3), but its pages are much better balanced overall.

The two designs share content and structure. In A, the Arabic counterpart of the school-visits callout is orphaned at the top of page 3, cut off from its English text on A2. B keeps it on the same page as its callout (B2), so the bilingual pair reads together. A's serif type and tighter column fill give a slightly fuller page, but B's continuity is the stronger reason to prefer it.

A gives each section its own page: Operations keeps text, stats and charts together, and both finance tables sit intact on one page. B splits the income statement across B4–B5 with a repeated header. It leaves B2 half empty, puts the chair's image at the top of the Operations page, and leaves B5 mostly blank. A's Arabic text is larger and better matched to the English.

A keeps the income statement in one table on A4, while B splits it across B4–B5 and repeats the header for only two rows. A's layout is more compact: the coloured header bands and consistent sans type tie it together. B leaves large empty areas on B2 and B5, and its full-bleed image on B3 crowds the next section.

A has a strong navy cover with a left-aligned title block, a refined serif with generous measure, and light rules above section heads. B's cover floats in the middle of a blank page. B's heavy navy header and footer bands repeat on every page, and its denser, hyphenated justified text feels crowded. The content and tables are otherwise near-identical.

A starts each section on its own page, so Finance's intro stays with its tables and the People feature stays with its section heading. B splits Finance across pages: the intro sits at the bottom of B3 and the tables follow on B4. B also strands the apprenticeship feature alone on B5 under a mostly empty page, cut off from its heading on B4. A's serif body text reads more comfortably, and its section headings carry more weight.

A has a navy cover with a teal rule that carries through the page-top bands. Its sections each get their own room. Its chart sits with its own commentary. B packs more onto each page: on B2 the chart is squeezed in, and B3 opens with an orphaned paragraph cut off from the chart it explains. B also uses an indented body against outdented heavy sans headings, which feels mismatched. The tables in the two designs are equivalent. A's main cost is the near-empty appendix page, A5.

A pairs bold numbered sans headings with a serif body, so the headings stand out clearly. B's light-weight headings are weak against its body text. The pink rules above each section in B add clutter, and B's light sans body with wide tracking reads less comfortably. Layout, metric strip and table are otherwise near-identical.

Design B fits the content into four pages. The image sits in-column on B3 with its caption, and the cover is unified. Design A leaves A3 half empty, runs the photo full-bleed on A4, and puts a lone paragraph on an otherwise blank A5, so its page rhythm is poor. A's serif body text is pleasant, but B's consistent rules and header band carry a clearer structure.

Design A keeps the school-visits Arabic translation on the same page as its English callout (A2), so each section stays together. Design B pushes that Arabic text to the top of page 3 without a heading (B3), which orphans it from the callout on B2. B's cover title is cleaner than A's awkward three-line wrap (A1), and its serif text is elegant. Still, A's consistent running headers and tighter page grouping read better overall.

A's cover is a clear, well-composed illustration with a solid title band. B's cover has a dull grey moon and the title sits over a busy wave pattern. A's English serif text is larger and pairs better with the Arabic. B's light Garamond-style body text looks small and thin next to its heavy Arabic. On B5 the pull-quote box covers the illustration and looks awkward. The tables and charts are essentially the same in both.

Design A keeps its title on one line in the header band, aligns headings and body to a single left edge, and adds a running header band on page 2 that ties the pages together. Design B has bolder headings, but its title breaks awkwardly onto two lines. B also outdents its headings past the body column, so the left edge looks ragged and unbalanced. Its page 2 drops the band and reads less coherently. Both tables are comparable.

B gives each section a clear start, with numbered headings and divider pages that carry a section navigator. Its tables sit together with their Finance text on B6. A packs Finance into the bottom of A3 and pushes its tables onto A4 under the People heading, so sections run across page breaks awkwardly. A5 is mostly empty. B's serif body text reads more comfortably. B's two near-empty divider pages are a cost, but its structure is clearer overall.

A pairs a refined serif with clear heading sizes and a calm full cover, and its charts are given readable height. On A4 the cash-cover line spans a usable range. B is clean but its heavy header and footer bands repeat on every page and add visual noise. Its light sans body with wide justified spacing reads thinner. Its charts are squashed: the B2 bar chart and the B3 line chart, which has only two y ticks, are hard to read.

A spreads content over five pages. Page A3 is half empty after a short paragraph. The full-bleed image on A4 pushes the section mid-page. A5 holds only one stranded paragraph and is otherwise blank. B fits the same content into four pages. Its image sits inline on B3, and Next steps stays together on B4. Its teal heading bands and running headers give a consistent rhythm. A's ruled serif headings are elegant and slightly more refined, but its pagination is clearly weaker.

A keeps the Arabic counterpart of the school-visits callout on page 2, right below the panel it translates. B pushes that Arabic paragraph to the top of page 3, cut off from its English pair and the image. A also has a solid header band and a cleaner sans text face that sets well with the Arabic. B's serif makes the narrow callout panel wrap into many short lines.

A keeps the content to four pages with an evenly sized Arabic column and well-integrated image placement. B leaves a half-empty page at B3 because the image is pushed to B4. It then spills a single orphaned paragraph onto a nearly blank B5. B's Arabic text is also noticeably smaller than its English, so the bilingual columns look unbalanced. B's cover with a white lower half is clean, but overall the flow is weaker.

Design B keeps each section together: the replanting paragraph stays with its river section on B3 instead of spilling onto A4. Its full-width image fills the column better than A's narrower inset (A3), and its heading bands give a steady structure. Design A's serif body text and numbered headings read a little more warmly, but the orphaned paragraph on A4 and the heavier page breaks weigh against it.

B's cover uses the full landscape illustration with a solid title band, which is clearer than A's dim, murky cover. On the inside pages, B's bold numbered sans headings and running headers with section names give stronger navigation. Its body text is larger and its Arabic is better matched to the Latin. A has a refined serif look but lighter, thinner headings and smaller text. The table and chart treatments are much the same in both.

B uses bold numbered headings and a serif body that make sections easy to scan. Its charts are larger and more legible (B3, B4), while A's charts are squat and compressed (A2, A3). A has a strong banded opening page (A1), and its light-weight headings are weaker in hierarchy. A also leaves large empty areas on A2 and A3. B's mostly empty cover page (B1) costs a page, but its content pages are better filled and more readable.

B keeps the allocation table whole on one page. A splits it across A2 and A3 with a repeated header, so the rows and the total sit apart. A has strong full-bleed section bands that give it more presence. Still, the broken table is a notable flaw. B's numbered headings and coherent page flow read cleanly, though B4 ends with a lot of empty space.

The two designs share the same structure. B pairs bold numbered sans headings with serif body text, which gives a clearer hierarchy and easier reading in a board paper. A uses light-weight headings with pink rules, and the headings sit weakly against the body text. A's grey text, set fully justified, also reads a little less comfortably than B's serif text. The tables and stat bands are essentially equal.

Design B packs the content into four well-filled pages. Its section headings are larger and numbered, and its running headers make the document easy to navigate. The image sits inside the text column with its caption, and the teal palette is used consistently across the cover band, table header and charts. Design A runs to five pages. Page A3 is half empty and page A5 holds a single orphaned paragraph. The full-bleed image on A4 is jammed against the body text, and the headings are small and set off-grid to the left. The one point in A's favour is its slightly crisper serif type.

B keeps the school-visits Arabic paragraph on the same page as its English callout. A pushes it to the top of page 3, cut off from its context. In B the callout sits beside the illustration rather than covering it, and running header bands give clear navigation. A's serif/Arabic pairing is elegant, and its title stacks cleanly where B's cover title wraps awkwardly. Even so, B's flow and continuity are stronger overall.

B keeps the allocation table whole on one page, while A splits it across pages with a repeated header (A2–A3). A's heavy full-bleed section bands chop the pages up. B's thin rules give a calmer, more consistent rhythm, though B4 runs a little sparse. B's cover is more muted but cohesive.

A's cover title sets English and Arabic on separate clean lines, while B wraps the Arabic awkwardly onto a third line after 'Commission |', weakening the masthead. A's refined serif and Arabic face pairing reads more elegantly than B's heavier body text, which wraps more often. B's running headers and colour block on page 2 are reasonable, but the cover flaw tips it to A.

B keeps the income statement whole on B4. A splits it across A4–A5 with a repeated header, and leaves A2 and A5 mostly empty. B's header and footer bands, gold section rules and consistent single-sans setting give steadier rhythm. B's apprentice callout sits beside the image on B5 instead of overlapping it as on A6. A's serif text has some typographic charm, and its cover is more open.

A pairs a bold sans heading face with a serif body, which gives clear contrast and a more refined reading texture. Its bold section heads stand out strongly. B uses light-weight heads in a single sans family, so the heads look weak against the body text. B adds a running header band and a fuller footer, but A's hierarchy and typographic contrast read better overall. The two designs share the same layout, tables and KPI row.

B gives Finance its own page with the tables directly under its heading. A puts the Finance heading at the bottom of A3 and splits it from the tables on A4. A4 also places the tables above the People and safety heading, so they read as part of the wrong section. B5 keeps People and safety together, with the image and quote overlay sitting under its own section. A5 has an orphaned image page with no heading. A's sans type is slightly crisper and its cover is brighter, but B's section structure and page rhythm are cleaner.

Design A leaves most of its pages empty. A1 is mostly blank below the mission. A4 holds only a small table orphaned from its Finance text on A3. Its section heading is outdented from the body text, and the callout box overlaps the building image on A3. Design B fits the same content into three well-filled pages. It aligns headings with the text column and pairs the callout panel cleanly beside the image on B2. It keeps the finance text and table together on B3, and it adds consistent header bands and page footers.

The two designs share the same content, tables and charts. A uses bold, numbered sans headings that stand out clearly, with consistent header and footer bands. B's light serif headings are weaker. Its appendix heading on B5 switches to a small bold style that does not match the other section heads, which breaks the hierarchy. B's dark cover on B1 is striking, but its title wraps awkwardly.

A keeps content compact across 3 pages with a consistent margin grid, running headers, and the finance table kept with its section. B leaves the cover mostly empty and pushes the hero image onto page 2, where it bleeds off the margins. B's headings hang left of the indented text. Its finance table is orphaned alone on page 4, separated from its heading.

A keeps its numbered sections in a consistent rhythm, with navy header and footer bands that carry running heads. Each chart sits beside its own commentary (A3, A4). B leaves the renewables commentary orphaned at the top of B3, away from the chart on B2. B also demotes the Appendix heading to a smaller style (B4) and uses a lighter, less consistent hierarchy. A's last page is sparse, but the overall structure is clearer.

A has more refined typefaces, but its headings hang left of the indented body text, so the page has two misaligned left edges. Its title breaks awkwardly across two lines, and its rules and spacing are heavy. B keeps headings and body on one aligned column, fits the title on one line, numbers its sections, and adds a header and footer to page 2. Its tinted metric figures and table rules tie the pages together, so B reads more cleanly and consistently.

A is a compact five-page document with consistent, elegant serif typography and a clean gold rule system. B adds two near-empty divider pages (B2, B5) whose sidebar navigation wastes space. B's chair page lacks a heading (B3), its section numbering is inconsistent, and its cover crowds the title into a heavy lower band. B's headers and footers are informative, but they don't offset the padding and broken rhythm.

A pairs a refined serif with a matched Arabic face at comfortable sizes, and the bilingual columns read evenly. B's heavier slab serif sets English larger than the small Arabic, so the paired columns look lopsided. B's cover crops the illustration into a hard band above a flat blue block. A's full-bleed cover holds the title more elegantly. B's running headers with section names are a small plus. Tables and charts are nearly identical in both designs.

A gives each section a divider page and its own content page, so every section opens cleanly. Its serif body text is comfortable to read. A's divider pages are sparse, and its chair page has an odd missing heading. B packs sections together instead. Finance starts at the foot of B3 and its tables carry over to B4 under a 'People and safety' running head. People and safety then splits across B4 and B5, with a mostly empty B5. A's structure is clearer and paced more evenly.

A fits the content into four pages and places the image inline beside its section. B leaves a large blank area on B3. It pushes the image to B4 away from its text and ends on B5 with an orphaned paragraph on a nearly empty page. A's numbered, larger section heads also give clearer hierarchy than B's small run-in heads.

A adds full divider pages with sidebar navigation (A2, A5), which give a strong structure, plus solid header and footer bands. B uses consistent section headings on every page with a lighter running header (B2–B5). Its page flow is tighter, with no near-empty divider pages, and it is easier to read and keep. A's divider pages are largely empty, and its chapter 1 title breaks awkwardly (A2). Content pages are otherwise nearly identical.

A keeps the river section intact on one page (A3), with the replanting paragraph staying under its photo and heading. B splits that section, pushing the replanting paragraph onto B4 with no heading, which breaks the section's continuity. A's coloured heading bands give a consistent rhythm through the report (A2–A4). B's plain numbered headings and serif body text read cleanly but are less distinctive.

A keeps the income statement whole on one page (A6), whereas B splits it across B4 and B5 and repeats the header. B also strands a full-bleed image above the Operations heading on B3, separated from the chair's text it belongs to. B5 is mostly empty. A uses divider pages and consistent running bands to give clearer section structure (A2, A5). Its tables and charts sit cleanly inside each section (A4, A6). A's divider pages do add some sparse space.

A keeps each section intact. Its elegant serif headings pair cleanly with the Arabic, and the pages breathe. B's full-bleed cover is striking, but page 2 crams three sections and a shrunken image together. B also splits the Programmes paragraph mid-sentence across pages, leaving an orphaned 'dhow construction alive in two yards.' The callout panel in B3 is also cramped. A's only weakness is the Arabic callout text spilling onto A3.

Design B's cover is more striking, but its body splits the Programmes paragraph across pages B2–B3, stranding "dhow construction alive in two yards" at the top of B3. B also packs four sections onto B2. Design A has an awkward wrapped Arabic title on A1 and an orphaned Arabic line at the top of A3, but its sections stay intact and it paces them more evenly, keeping the Programmes text whole on A2.

B keeps the income statement whole on one page (B4), while A splits it across pages and repeats the header (A4–A5). B also avoids A's near-empty chair page (A2) and the large gap at the foot of A5. B's running header and footer, its consistent navy accents and its full-colour cover band (B1) make it feel more unified. B's callout panel sits beside the image instead of covering it (B5 vs A6). A's mixed sans and serif headings are crisper, but A's layout is more fragmented overall.

A uses a unified serif system with a single-line title and headings aligned to the body column, so it reads as one calm, coherent column. B hangs its bold sans headings out to the left of the indented body text, which creates two left edges. B's title also breaks awkwardly to leave 'Paper' alone on a line, and its body text is lighter and more condensed. A's crimson rule and band carry onto page 2 and give it consistent rhythm.

B pairs a bold sans heading with serif body text, which gives its headings stronger hierarchy than A's light headings. B also fills its pages evenly and keeps the chart beside its table on B2. A ends with a nearly empty last page (A4) and leaves large voids on A2 and A3. A's banded header and footer are more polished, and its cover band combined with the highlights is efficient. Still, B's cover is clean and its pacing is better overall.

A adds two near-empty divider pages that are mostly blank (A2, A5) and uses heavy full-width header and footer bars. Its cover splits the illustration and the title band awkwardly (A1). B is tighter, with five pages, an integrated cover where the title sits over the landscape (B1), consistent light gold rules, and the pull-quote overlaid on the image (B5). A's stronger bold headings help hierarchy slightly, but overall B reads more cohesively and with less wasted space.

B's full-bleed cover image (B1) makes a strong cover, and its pages flow evenly with no large voids. A ends on a page that is two-thirds empty (A3), and its cover title breaks awkwardly across three lines with the Arabic stranded (A1). B splits the Programmes paragraph across pages (B2–B3), and its slightly heavier headings help A a little on hierarchy. Overall B is more balanced.

A packs the same content into four pages with strong bold sans headings and an indented body that gives clear hierarchy. Its pages are evenly filled. B has a striking navy cover and accent bands, but its light serif headings are weaker. Its flow is also uneven: the chart is split from its table, B2 and B5 are left half-empty, and the appendix is stranded on a mostly blank last page.

B's bold numbered sans headings stand out clearly against the serif body text, and its running header and footer help navigation. A uses light serif headings with red rules above them. They read weaker and are more decorative, and the rule above every section breaks up page 2. A's justified lines are wider and show some uneven spacing. Tables and stat callouts are essentially the same in both.
